preamble: In Chamorro, the Austronesian language of the Mariana Islands, Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *z regularly became the voiceless affricate written ⟨ch⟩, which is usually pronounced [ts] (with [tʃ] before non-low front vowels). PMP *z is reconstructed by Blust as the voiced postalveolar affricate /dʒ/ (a voiced palatal affricate); some treatments write it /ɟ͡ʝ/. The change combines devoicing with depalatalization of the affricate. Neighbouring Palauan instead turned *z into a flap r.

examples.note: Palauan rayl 'road' shows the r reflex of the same etymon.

examples.to: chahan 'cook in an underground pit; pit oven'

sources: Blust, R. & Trussel, S. (2020). Austronesian Comparative Dictionary: Sets z. https://ling.lll.hawaii.edu/dicts/ACD/acd-s_z.htm
Wikipedia (2026). Chamorro language: Phonology and historical sound changes. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chamorro_language
